openQuestions: Official name in English and Ukrainian, canonical domain and postal address, from the official site and the EDEBO register.
Dated official statement for the current academic year on whether, where and how foreign students are taught.
State registration (EDEBO), programme licence (Ministry or EDEBO licence register) and NAQA accreditation for each health programme: three separate claims.
Which medicine, dentistry, pharmacy or nursing programmes admit foreign applicants, in which language, with what duration and intake, and the official fee page.

Location lead as found (unverified): Kyiv (lead: search summary of ieu.edu.ua/for-foreign-students/about-university gives "42B Akademika Hlushkova avenue, Kyiv"; vstup.osvita.ua 2025 lists the institution in Kyiv with programme dates 01.10.2025–01.07.2030, i.e. no relocation shown)

Relocation lead (unverified): No Ukrainian relocation reported: the 2025 admissions-portal cards place the Medicine programme in Kyiv with term 01.10.2025–01.07.2030 and NAQA recorded a May 2025 decision. Contradictory foreign claim: The Shift (Malta, undated page ?p=104535) states "Since the war in Ukraine, the IEU has transferred its operations to Poland. However, the Polish government never officially recognised it, and the public prosecutor of Poznan is reportedly investigating it" — this is a single-outlet claim about overseas branches, not about the Kyiv licence, and is unverified. The Malta branch (Gzira) lost its MFHEA temporary licence on 13 Aug 2025.

Red flag to resolve before any fact is shown: Malta branch licence revoked: MFHEA announcement dated 13 Aug 2025 states 'the temporary licence granted to International European University (Licence No. 2023-016) has been revoked' and IEU 'will no longer be authorised to operate as a university in Malta' (mfhea.mt/?p=1350). The Shift (14 Aug 2025) reports the audit found IEU 'failing to meet nine out of eleven standards' and calls it a 'sham university'; 52 students appealed visa cancellations (20 Aug 2025). These concern the Maltese operation, not the Ukrainian licence, but the brand is the same.

Red flag to resolve before any fact is shown: Poland claim (The Shift, undated): operations 'transferred to Poland', 'never officially recognised' by the Polish government, Poznan prosecutor 'reportedly investigating' — single-outlet, unverified; any IEU 'European campus' marketing to applicants should not be presented as Ukrainian-licensed study.

Red flag to resolve before any fact is shown: Admissions-portal card shows the Medicine master's entering 'на базі: Молодший спеціаліст' (junior specialist) — unusual structure for a 222 Medicine programme; needs the official rules of admission to confirm entry basis for foreign school-leavers.
Red flag to resolve before any fact is shown: Dentistry, Pharmacy and Nursing: no lead at all; the directory must list only Medicine 222 unless EDEBO shows more.

Red flag to resolve before any fact is shown: Name confusion: not the same as Kyiv International University (KIU, Wikipedia result), European University (Європейський університет, Kyiv, a different private university) or Kyiv Medical University (KMU). Also distinct from 'Міжнародний грецький університет' (irrelevant result).
Red flag to resolve before any fact is shown: Reported owner via TOV 'Polimed-K' (Serhii Ryzhkov, share capital UAH 14.2m) comes from an undated Interfax item; currency unknown.
Red flag to resolve before any fact is shown: Contact leads are inconsistent: search title shows '+38 063 169 98 67', summary cites foreign students department '+380507133624'.

Red flag to resolve before any fact is shown: Inventory flag carried forward: 'licence questions' — the only state-recognition lead is the NAQA accreditation summary; the MON licence order/licensed volume for 222 Medicine was not found.
